traits.habitat_notes: Roadsides, waste ground, gravel pits and shores, arable land (FNA, introduced); meadows and scrub (FOC).

taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form chosen from the plant's habit: a loose clump of grey-green leafy stems from a taprooted crown, each ending in a forking cyme of white flowers with inflated bladder calyces.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species.

allometry.note: 0.6 m tall at 3 years in the open, inside the floras' range of heights, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Every look comes from the characters through the library's rules: a loose clump of grey-green leafy stems from a taprooted crown, each ending in a forking cyme of white flowers with inflated bladder calyces.

traits.library_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): plants short-lived perennial herbs with a woody caudex: a forb.

traits.life_span.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): plants short-lived perennial; FOC herbs perennial.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stems herbaceous from a woody caudex and stout taproot (FOC roots slightly lignified).

traits.stem_posture.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stems several to many, erect, branched and decumbent at the base: curving up from a leaning foot.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stems 20-80 cm. FOC gives 40-100 cm tall, taken as the high; Wikipedia says to 60 cm.

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of China vol. 6 (2001), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): 40-100 cm tall.

traits.crown_width_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: a clump of several to many decumbent-based stems from one caudex spreads about as wide as the plant is tall, to some 0.6 m.

traits.stem_cross_section.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene (Morton) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stems terete or sometimes angular; no angles named for S. vulgaris.

traits.stem_hairs.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): glabrous, rarely pubescent; FOC glabrous throughout.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): glabrous, rarely pubescent.

traits.rosette.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves mainly cauline.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves 2 per node.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Flora of China vol. 6 (2001), Caryophyllaceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves opposite, decussate.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade broadly oblong to oblanceolate or lanceolate, rarely nearly linear; FOC lanceolate to ovate.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade 2-8 cm long; FOC 4-10 cm, the 10 kept as high.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade 5-30 mm wide; FOC 1-3(-4.5) cm, the 4.5 as high.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves sessile, almost clasping.

traits.leaf_base_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): base round; FOC: proximal leaves attenuate at base, distal leaves cuneate and slightly clasping.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): apex acute to acuminate; FOC acuminate or acute.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): margins entire.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): plants glaucous; FOC 'grayish green'; sRGB by eye for the words.

traits.stem_colour.note: Flora of China vol. 6 (2001), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stems usually gray; with FNA's glaucous plant, a grey-green; sRGB by eye for the words.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): inflorescence an open dichasial cyme; FOC many-flowered dichasia, sometimes thyrsoid.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): cyme 5-40-flowered.

traits.pedicel_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pedicels 0.5-3 cm; FOC: shorter than or about equal to the calyx.

traits.flower_posture.note: Flora of China vol. 6 (2001), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers sometimes spreading or slightly nodding.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers 15-20 mm across; Wikipedia: to 1.8 cm wide.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene (Morton) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): calyx 5-lobed, petals 5.

traits.perianth.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene (Morton) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals joined into a tube; petals 5, clawed.

traits.petal_length_m.note: Flora of China vol. 6 (2001), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals 1.5-1.8 cm; FNA petals about twice as long as the calyx.

traits.petal_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): limb obovate; FOC limb obovate, lobes narrowly obovate.

traits.petal_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): limb emarginate to 2-lobed; FOC deeply bifid to the base of the limb.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals white; sRGB by eye for the word.

traits.sepal_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): calyx 9-12 mm in flower, 12-18 mm in fruit; FOC 1.3-1.6 cm, the 16 mm as high.

traits.calyx_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): calyx pale green, rarely purplish (FOC usually violet-tinged), papery and inflated with a net of veins; sRGB by eye for 'pale green'.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene (Morton) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens 10.

traits.stamen_exsertion.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens exserted by 2-4 mm; FOC stamens and styles prominently exserted.

traits.anther_colour.note: Flora of China vol. 6 (2001), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): anthers violet; sRGB by eye for the word.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): styles 3; FOC styles 3.

traits.pistil_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): styles cream to greenish, at most slightly pink-tinged; sRGB by eye for the words.

traits.sexual_system.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): some plants bear bisexual flowers, others pistillate flowers only (gynodioecious). The vocabulary has no gynodioecy; 'polygamous' (bisexual and unisexual flowers) is the nearest state.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): capsules ovoid to globose, opening by 6 teeth.

traits.fruit_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): capsules ovoid to globose; FOC subglobose.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of China vol. 6 (2001), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): capsule subglobose, about 8 mm across, shorter than the calyx. (FNA: capsule equalling the calyx.)

traits.capsule_valves.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): capsule opening by 6 teeth.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): calyx inflated, 9-12 mm in flower growing to 12-18 x 7-11 mm in fruit: it enlarges round the capsule.

traits.fruiting_calyx_posture.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): the inflated calyx encloses the capsule (capsule equalling the calyx; FOC capsule shorter than the calyx).

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: a ripe dry capsule straw to pale brown inside the papery bladder; sRGB by eye.

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of China vol. 6 (2001), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowering June-August, fruiting August-September; FNA flowering summer-fall in North America, so September added.

traits.fruiting_months.note: Flora of China vol. 6 (2001), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruiting August-September; October added for FNA's fall flowering.

traits.elevation_min_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): 0-2000 m in North America.

traits.elevation_max_m.note: Flora of China vol. 6 (2001), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): 200-2700 m in China; FNA to 2000 m.

traits.light.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): roadsides, waste ground, gravel pits, arable land: open places.

traits.moisture.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): roadsides, gravel pits and shores, arable land; FOC meadows and scrub. Read as mesic to dry.

traits.habitat_notes.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Silene vulgaris (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): habitats as listed; introduced across most of North America from Europe.

traits.shoot_leaves.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read counts it: FNA and Flora of China describe leafy stems 20-80 cm with opposite pairs, so about 8 pairs on a stem.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read counts it: a loose forking cyme of 5-30 flowers on 1-2 cm pedicels, so 5-15 cm.

traits.flowering_branches.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read counts it: the cyme forks from the top one or two pairs of leaves.
